rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He frames the passage as instruction for new Muslims not yet mature in faith; earnest instruction in right is not slander or backbiting.
rows.anchor: henüz imanın bu yüksek zevkine erecek kadar terbiye almamış olanlara bu tehzîbi vermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported occasion concerns Banū Asad b. Khuzayma, who came during famine seeking booty, professed Islam, invoked their restraint from fighting the Prophet and family burdens, sought alms, and tried to make him indebted.
rows.anchor: Medine civarında Benî Esed b. Huzeyme kabilesi ganimet hevesiyle Müslümanlığa girmişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith requires more than verbal profession: inward assent with love, firmness, and tranquility; the Bedouins had not attained this.
rows.anchor: iman yalnız dil ile ikrardan ibaret değil, yürekten sevgi ile vüsuk ve itmi’nâna mukārin tasdik olmak lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here Islam means an outward profession and entry into peace or submission; that can be true without firm inward assent, while claiming faith without it is false.
rows.anchor: silme duhûl ve inkıyâd mânasına islâm muharebeyi terkedip de zâhirde ikrar vermekle hâsıl olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delicate wording avoids bluntly prohibiting the claim of faith or conclusively affirming their legally recognized faith; it instead directs them to describe outward submission.
rows.anchor: nazmın üslûbu bu nâzik şekle ifrağ edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi resolves the Sunni equation of believer and Muslim by distinguishing general from particular: faith is inward, Islam broader, though they coincide in a particular case.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî burada “mü’min ile müslim Ehl-i Sünnete göre birdir. [^20] Nasıl olup da burada bu fark anlaşılabiliyor?” diye sorarak

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib distinguishes Islam below faith as verbal acknowledgment that protects life, and above faith as profession joined to belief, fidelity, and surrender to God’s decree.
rows.anchor: Râgıb da Müfredât’ında şöyle der: “İslâm, şer‘de iki kısımdır. Birisi imanın dûnundadır ki bu, lisan ile itiraftır.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam
rows.claim: The Fiqh al-Akbar attributed to Abu Hanifa defines faith as confession and assent, Islam as surrender and obedience; legally they are inseparable, while religion names faith, Islam, and sharia together.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam’a mensub Fıkh-ı Ekber’de de şöyle mezkurdur: “İman, ikrar ve tasdiktir, İslâm Allah teâlâ’nın emirlerine teslim ve inkıyaddır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam’s lexical senses from silm, salāma, and its hamza include entering peace, making safe, being safe, sincerity, surrender, and obedience; legal usage retains some lexical distinctions while stressing their joint realization.
rows.anchor: “islâm” kelimesi lügatta madde-i asliyesi olan silm ü selâmet ve hemzesinin duhûl ve ta‘diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the familiar sense Islam and faith are equal in realization and mutually entailed, with inward sincerity and outward submission; 4:94 supports treating believer and Muslim as one.
rows.anchor: Buna ma‘nâ-yı mârufuyla islâm demek muvâfık olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second legal sense makes Islam broader than faith: a preliminary verbal profession below faith, which is its goal; this verse calls it formal Muslimness, an entry into true Islam.
rows.anchor: Bu henüz Müslümanlık değil, Müslümanlığa bir giriştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sense makes Islam higher than faith, a perfection including ihsan (2:112), the reality of 3:19, and the God-consciousness encouraged in 49:13.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü: İmandan ehas ve onun bir kemâli, bir gayesi olmak üzere fevkinde olan islâmdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience means advancing from outward profession to sincere faith and gladly acting on God’s and the Messenger’s commands; God fully rewards, forgives, and adds grace.
rows.anchor: kalben de ihlâs ile imana terakkī edip mü’min-i kâmil ve müslim-i sâdık olmak üzere mûcebince amel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith requires casting doubt out initially and remaining free of doubt for faith to endure.
rows.anchor: iman etmek için ibtidâ kalbden şüpheyi atmak şart olduğu gibi ileride bekāsı için de şüpheden âzâde olmak şarttır

words: وَجَٰهَدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striving with wealth and lives means bearing hardships in obedience and includes every form of financial and bodily worship.
rows.anchor: Emvâl ve enfüs ile mücahede mâlî ve bedenî her türlü ibâdâta şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are truthful in claiming faith because their hearts and deeds fulfill their profession.
rows.anchor: İman iddiasında sâdık, verdikleri ikrâra kalbleriyle ve fiilleriyle sadakat etmiş hâlis Müslümanlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you teach God your religion?” rebukes the Bedouins for presuming to inform Him of their piety.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet o a‘râbîleri tevbihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minnet is a gift given without expectation of reward to meet a need, leaving lasting gratitude; mentioning it reproaches the recipient.
rows.anchor: onu veren verdiği kimseden hiçbir sevap istemez, yalnız onun ihtiyâcını kesmek ister

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He derives favor and recounting it from cutting: a gift cuts off need, speech cuts off the gift and the gratitude it calls for.
rows.anchor: İkisi de kesmek mânasına “menn”den me’huzdur. İn‘âm fiili ihtiyâcı keser, söylemek de nimeti keser

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib instead derives minnet from the weight measure mann, a heavy favor done by giving; he cites 3:164, 4:94, 37:114, 14:11, and 28:5 and says this act truly belongs to God.
rows.anchor: Râgıb, bu menn ü minnetin evzândan olan batman mânasına “menn”den me’huz olduğuna kāil

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib says verbal minnet burdens its recipient and is ugly among people, except in reproach for ingratitude; he cites sayings that it destroys a good deed and is fitting when a gift is denied.
rows.anchor: İkincisi de söz ile olur, o ağırlık laf ile verilir ki insanlar arasında bu çirkin sayılır.

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib reads the Bedouins’ minnet as spoken, but God’s minnet as the act of guiding them.
rows.anchor: onlardan olan minnet kavil ile, Allah’tan onlara olan minnet de fiil iledir ki onlara hidâyetidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions Raghib: here God’s minnet should be a verbal warning about ingratitude, since an enacted favor has no warning force and this follows a prohibition in a warning context.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın bu son sözü cây-i nazardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must not boast of becoming Muslim: guidance to faith is God’s great favor, and boasting instead of thanking God risks divine reproach and loss of blessing.
rows.anchor: de onu Peygamber’in başına kakarsanız Allah teâlâ bu hidâyete karşı küfrânınızdan dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is a tremendous gift from God; the conditional tests whether their inner state matches their outward claim.
rows.anchor: iman çok büyük bir nimet, buna hidâyet Allah’tan bir minnet

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their inner and outer selves, sincerity, hearts, intentions, and what they will encounter.
rows.anchor: İslâmınızda sâdık olup olmadığınızı, kalblerinizde iman ve sadakat bulunup bulunmadığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees every deed and misses none, so people should correct themselves and act accordingly.
rows.anchor: Allah bütün amellerinize basîrdir her ne yaparsanız hepsini görür, hiçbirini kaçırmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies Sūrat Qāf as Meccan with forty-five verses.
rows.anchor: سُورَةُ قۤ مَ ِّكي َّةٌ وَهِيَ خمَْسٌ وَأَرْبـَعُونَ اٰيَةً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering emphasizes an oath by God’s majesty: We created the human and know its whispers, nearer than the jugular vein.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Hem şânıma kasem ederim ki hakikat insanı Biz yarattık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation recalls the first creation, prepares what follows, and serves as an inference to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bu ihtar hem halk-ı evveli takrir hem de mâba‘dine temhiddir, hem ilmin isbâtına halktan bir istidlâl

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation reminder teaches transcendence so the statement of nearness does not confuse Creator and creature.
rows.anchor: akrebiyetten bahsolunurken hâlık ile mahlûku karıştırmamak için bir tenzih delîlini telkindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul’s whisperings include all inward consciousness: self-talk, feelings, imaginings, memories, fancies, and decisions.
rows.anchor: gizli duygular, vehimler, hâtıralar, kuruntular, kararlar gibi bütün bâtınî şuur şuûnâtına şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows hidden thoughts unknown even to the recording angels, because He created them.
rows.anchor: hafaza meleklerinin bile henüz vâkıf olmadığı derecede gizli olarak insanın gönlüne gelen hâtırat

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows, reaches, and acts upon the human with the immediacy of nearness beyond the jugular.
rows.anchor: Öyle yakından bilir, öyle yakından yetişir, icrâ-yı te’sîr ederiz

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator’s relation precedes the creature’s relation to itself, since the creature exists by God’s power; he links this to 2:186.
rows.anchor: Hâlık ile mahlûku arasındaki nisbet, mahluk ile nefsi arasındaki nisbetten daha mukaddemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes veins returning blood toward the heart from arteries carrying it outward, and describes black blood passing through the right heart and lungs, where it meets air and becomes red before returning to the left heart.
rows.anchor: Teşrihte iki nevi damar sayarlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the described circuits great and small circulation; arterial blood is red and venous black in the great circuit, reversed in the small.
rows.anchor: Deverân-ı kebîrde şiryanlarda kırmızı, verîdlerde siyah kan vardır. Deverân-ı sağīrde ise şiryanlarda siyah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus red arterial and black venous blood are not universal labels; veins are black-blood vessels only generally.
rows.anchor: verîdlere “siyah kan damarları” denmesi küllî değil, ekseriyet itibariyledir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines the dual veridan as vessels along the front of the neck, connected to the vetin, carrying blood from the head.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ta der ki: “El-verîdân boynun önünde iki safhasını kavramış iki damardır

rows.speaker: İbn Esîr
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir says the verid is a front-neck vessel that swells in anger; Elmalılı notes the jugular sense properly uses the dual.
rows.anchor: İbn Esîr de Nihâye’de “verîd, boynun yüzündeki damardır ki gazab hâlinde şişer

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib defines the verid as a vessel connected to the liver and heart, containing blood channels.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Râgıb şöyle ifade etmiştir: “Verîd, kebide ve kalbe muttasıl olur bir damardır

rows.speaker: Nizamüddîn Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Nisaburi defines verid as a blood-carrying vessel, unlike arteries, and veridan as the pair of vessels at the front of the neck joining the vetin.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddîn Nîsâbûrî de Garâibü’l-Kur’ân nâm tefsirinde “verîd, şerâyînin gayrı olarak demi hâmil damardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habl means rope or bond and can mean vessel; most take habl al-warid as the vein, a general-to-specific construction.
rows.anchor: ip ve bağ demektir. Damar mânasına

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari allows habl to mean the base of the neck, making a lāmī genitive and permitting a metaphor for neck or body.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî bu mâna ile lâmî izâfeti de tecviz eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive can be a simile: the vein is imagined as a rope around the neck.
rows.anchor: izâfet-i teşbîhiyye ile “verîd ipi”, boyuna dolanmış ipe benzeyen verîd mefhûmunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since verid is singular but generic, the phrase may mean the whole vein network or the vena cava.
rows.anchor: Verîd müfred olmak itibariyle cinse hamlolunmak lâzım geleceği cihetle

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib takes habl al-warid to mean the spirit.
rows.anchor: Râgıb, “habl-i verîd”den murad rûh olduğuna kāil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vein is apt because it gathers blood toward the heart, unlike outward-flowing arteries; the poet uses it as a proverb for nearness, meaning nearer than one’s closest vessel or life.
rows.anchor: Nitekim şâir وَالْمَوْتُ أَدْنَى لَهُ مِنَ الْوَرِيدِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vein’s black blood returns used cells to the heart for purification, hinting at renewed creation and the afterlife discussed next.
rows.anchor: kullanılmış, ölmüş hüceyreleri hâmil olan bir siyah kanın kalbe vürûdu bir tasfiye ile yeni bir halka
